ex.en: a task which requires skill

groups.etymology: Inherited from Old French existence, from Late Latin existentia (“existence”).
From Latin existō.

senses.d: to post, to send, to ship
to deal with quickly, to get rid of

groups.etymology: From expédi(ent) + -er.

ex.fr: expérience de pensée
ex.en: thought experiment

ex.fr: expérience de mort imminente
ex.en: near-death experience

ex.fr: faire l'expérience de quelque chose
ex.en: to experience something

ex.fr: L'expérience est souvent un critère important pour l'embauche.
ex.en: Experience is often an important criteria when job hunting.

groups.etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin experientia.
Learned borrowing from Latin explicātiōnem.
From Middle French expliquer (14th c.), a borrowing from Latin explicāre. Doublet of éployer.

senses.d: to explode (fly apart with sudden violent force)

groups.etymology: From Latin explosiōnem, accusative singular of explosiō.
Inherited from Middle French exposer, borrowed from Latin expōnere, contaminated by and conjugated like French poser. Compare Old French espondre, which was inherited.
Learned borrowing from Latin expressus.

ex.fr: C’est clair qu’il l’a fait exprès.
ex.en: It’s obvious that he did it on purpose.

ex.fr: Excusez-moi, je ne l’ai pas fait exprès.
ex.en: Excuse me, I didn't do it on purpose.

senses.d: a messenger carrying letters for personal delivery

groups.etymology: Inherited from Middle French expression, borrowed from Latin expressiōnem (“a pressing out”).

ex.fr: Je me suis mal exprimé.
ex.en: I misspoke.

ex.fr: Il lui est parfois difficile de s'exprimer clairement à cause de sa forme particulière d'intelligence.
ex.en: It's sometimes difficult for him to express himself clearly because of his peculiar form of intelligence.

groups.etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin exprimere. Compare the inherited doublet épreindre.

ex.fr: Laissant de côté la physiologie végétale, nous nous bornerons à l'étude des éléments extérieurs.
ex.en: Leaving plant physiology aside, we shall confine ourselves to the study of external elements.

groups.etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin extraordinārius.

ex.fr: Il vivait dans l'extrême pauvreté à l'époque.
ex.en: He had lived in extreme poverty at the time.

groups.etymology: Inherited from Middle French extreme, extrême, borrowed from Latin extrēmus.

ex.fr: d'un extrême à un autre
ex.en: from one extreme to another

ex.fr: Les extrêmes se touchent.
ex.en: Extremes meet.

groups.etymology: From extrême + -ment.

senses.d: tip; end; top (furthermost or highest part)

ex.fr: Sa tige souterraine, ou rhizome, s'allonge chaque année, portant un rameau aérien vers son extrémité.
ex.en: Its underground stem, or rhizome, elongates each year, bearing an aerial shoot near its tip.
